note: Ground truth for the eval harness (Phase 6). Never readable by packages/agents or apps/server. Times are virtual microseconds from simulation start.

rootCause.summary: The checkout v2.4.1 deploy exhausted the shared DB connection pool.
rootCause.mechanism: checkout holds one pooled connection for its order transaction while it calls inventory and payment, which need connections from the same pool (hold-and-wait). The deploy raised checkout workers 20 -> 60 and stock reservation fan-out 1 -> 4 with the pool still at 30. Demand rose to about 90% of the pool, queries began to wait, waiting kept transactions open longer, and with 60 workers checkout could hold all 30 connections while its own downstream queries starved.

causalChain.step: DB connection pool reaches 30/30 and a wait queue forms
db.pool.acquire waits grow to seconds and hit the 5 s acquire timeout in inventory, payment and checkout
checkout requests fail or take many seconds; all 60 checkout workers are busy, its queue fills and it rejects requests
api-gateway returns 5xx for checkout; stock requests slow to seconds because they share the pool

discriminatingEvidence: pool_in_use equals pool_capacity and pool_wait_queue grows right after the deploy, not before
db.pool.acquire spans dominate the latency of slow traces
db.query execution time per statement is unchanged; db_active_queries drops; the DB executor queue stays empty
db.transaction spans in checkout stay open for seconds while child calls wait for connections
stock requests, which never touch checkout, also wait on db.pool.acquire

redHerrings.whyNotCausal: No inventory request comes near either limit; reverting it leaves every request, span and metric identical.
Self-resolving 2.5 minutes before the incident; no errors; pool never stays saturated.

rejectedAlternatives.contradictedBy: per-statement query execution time is flat and the DB runs fewer queries than at baseline
payment latency is back to baseline 2.5 minutes before the incident

rejectedAlternatives.hypothesis: The inventory config change caused it
rejectedAlternatives.contradictedBy: no metric changes after ev_1; onset follows ev_2 within seconds

resolves.expected: errors ~0; p99 above baseline because the DB executor becomes the next bottleneck

partial.expected: no timeouts; latency bounded around 1 s; roughly a fifth of requests shed with fast 503s

worsens.expected: connections are held longer; higher latency, more failures
